text: To give a reservoir a target spectral radius rho_target, the ESN code first builds a random matrix W and then:
choices: multiplies W by rho_target / rho(W), preserving its structure while setting the spectral radius exactly to rho_target
adds rho_target to every diagonal entry of W
clips each eigenvalue of W individually to rho_target
retrains W by gradient descent until rho(W) equals rho_target
explanation: The standard rescaling is W_rec = (rho_target / rho(W)) * W, where rho(W) = max|eigvals(W)|. Multiplying by a scalar multiplies every eigenvalue by that scalar, so the new spectral radius is exactly rho_target while the sparsity pattern and relative structure are untouched. No diagonal shift, per-eigenvalue clipping, or gradient training is involved.
